S.name: A cheap checker of action validity
S.detail: Each edit is linted before it is applied, and removing the linter lowers SWE-bench Lite resolve rate 18.0% -> 15.0% (2405.15793#s2).

S.name: Route checked against a grounded obstacle
S.detail: Waypoint polylines are checked for clearance against a segmentation-grounded obstacle with phases cut at contact events; adding the route harness raises safe success 31.3 -> 60.6 and 18.8 -> 64.4 over 32 tasks for two models (2609.20822#s1).

S.name: STOP gated on usable depth and reliable detection
S.detail: STOP requests pass an identity, fresh-depth and completion check: +2.0 SR on R2R and HM3D-OVON subsets, and the OSR-SR gap narrows 22.0 -> 10.0 on HM3D-v2 (2609.15195#s3).

S.name: Accurate completion monitor
S.detail: A success detector ends executor runs: 57.39% long-horizon vs 52.36% with a fixed 8 s horizon and 43.50% with a VLM-predicted horizon, robust to 10% injected detection error (2606.10267#s1); executors that report invocation progress cut runtime VLM calls per episode from 109.5 to 1.988 (2605.13119#s2).

S.name: Diagnostics run after scoring in a resettable simulator
S.detail: Diagnostic programs run after scoring and before reset: final success 75% (45/60) vs 31.7%, completion-assessment precision 90.0% vs 43.2% (2610.12549#s1).

F.name: Checker is a weak proxy for success
F.detail: The linter misses 52% of unresolved instances (wrong implementations); a STOP gate passes at fresh depth 1.20 m vs goal distance 2.15 m and the OSR-SR gap stays 19.0 on HM3D-OVON; a box-only verifier on an approximately measured scene misses unmodeled constraints (2405.15793#s2, 2609.15195#s3, 2609.20822#s1).

F.name: Detector false positives and privileged detectors
F.detail: False-positive rates of 30-50% sharply hurt, correlated false negatives can stall a command, and the simulation detector reads privileged state (2606.10267#s1).

F.name: Gate contribution not isolated
F.detail: Proposal validation alone is not ablated; teacher-side search tools are ablated only as a bundle, with an extra GPU and one run per task (2609.15195#s1, 2609.27308#s2).

F.name: Added control tools lower success
F.detail: Checkpoint and search tools raise one model's mean score 0.66 -> 0.70 while its success falls 50% -> 43% (2609.27308#s2).

F.name: Planner gains depend on executor fidelity
F.detail: A planner over a plain SFT VLA hurts on LIBERO-Long (-0.2/-11.8/-12.0); the real study is one robot and one camera (2605.13119#s2).

F.name: Only valid with resets
F.detail: Diagnostics need resettable simulation and do not apply to single-shot real episodes; Cabinet stays at 40% with 10 trials per task (2610.12549#s1).

S.name: Model-by-harness grid with paired statistics
S.detail: Harness variance 18.48 pp^2 vs model variance 2.37 pp^2 (7.80x), with 6 of 9 ranking comparisons reversing (2605.23950#s1); tokens per solved task vary ~40x across harnesses vs 1.0-1.3x across models (2607.22585#s1); a post-hoc interaction with label-permutation p=0.003 (BH q=0.013) (2609.11987#s1).

S.name: One component toggled with typed interfaces fixed
S.detail: Variants differ only in the chosen module: memory gains are mediated by the reasoner (8.54 -> 30.67 with ReAct) (2606.14674#s1); scenes, seeds and backbone are fixed across safety-harness layers (2609.20822#s3).

S.name: Same-backbone reruns on fixed episodes
S.detail: Baselines rerun with the same model on the same 100 episodes: harness gaps of +11/+6/+22 SR across three backbones (2606.10577#s4) and +14.0/+18.0 SR (2609.15195#s4).

S.name: Repeated runs with endpoints and per-task patterns
S.detail: Six runs per task: 62 tasks always succeed, 8 always fail, 30 are mixed (2609.29861#s2); no-action turns 2.0-2.16 vs 0.2-0.3 per task replicate across models (2607.22585#s2).

S.name: Cost reconciled against billing
S.detail: Re-pricing raw usage corrects cache share to 87-98% (vs 48% under a double-count defect) and matches billed spend within 2-4% for one provider (2609.11987#s3).

F.name: Differences within noise
F.detail: 50 tasks (1 task = 2 pp) leave most pass-rate differences within noise; intervals 11-17 pp wide leave moderate effects undetectable (2607.22585#s1, 2609.11987#s1).

F.name: Cumulative harness layers
F.detail: Compared harnesses are cumulative, so per-layer contributions are not isolated, and the 7.80x ratio is stated as not universal (2605.23950#s1).

F.name: Single embodied runs without cost
F.detail: Embodied swaps are single runs without variance; harness gain varies 6-22 SR with the backbone and no cost is reported (2609.15195#s4, 2606.10577#s4).

F.name: Complete systems compared
F.detail: Serving and context handling differ across harnesses, and workflow vs agent is confounded with the action interface (strong models drop 82.3 -> 65 in a fixed workflow) (2607.26148#s3); hierarchy components swing success ~95% -> ~0% even with a near-perfect VLA proxy (2606.10267#s4).

F.name: Decomposition descriptive, not causal
F.detail: Attribution is co-movement; the category-assignment procedure is unspecified; persistent failures are not tied to causes or interventions (2605.23950#s2, 2606.14674#s3, 2609.29861#s2).

F.name: Ablations on the wrong model
F.detail: Harness ablations are run on base models only, not on the distilled student (a 2B model reaches 2.2% in the same harness) (2606.18363#s1).

F.name: Budget endings and missing usage
F.detail: 22 of 81 ceiling-cancelled runs had a passing patch (2609.11987#s2); 58 runs lack usage records and cache-write pricing is uncertain by ~2x (2609.11987#s3).

S.name: Bounded window with pull-based recall
S.detail: Context is a short window plus recall tools rather than accumulated history: removing the recall tool drops SR 76 -> 64, and accumulating all historical images lowers SR to 66 (SPL -12.45) (2606.10577#s3).

S.name: Memory variants compared with model and episodes fixed
S.detail: Event memory adds +7.0 SR on both R2R and HM3D-OVON with the model and 100 episodes fixed (2609.15195#s2).

S.name: Notes used where tasks recur
S.detail: Same tasks repeated across episodes or sharing subgoals with a reference seed: a summary of previous episodes raises long-horizon success 52.36% -> 60.00% (2606.10267#s3), and target-setting memory raises LIBERO-Pro Goal-S 31.0% -> 87.0% (2607.08448#s2).

S.name: Skill library with the model fixed and demo scenes disjoint
S.detail: LIBERO-Pro average 28.9% (no skills) -> 43.3% (seed) -> 75.6% (evolved) with the model fixed and demonstration scenes disjoint from evaluation (2609.29964#s2); a library mined from success-filtered programs improves average success (2603.22435#s2).

S.name: Replay cards for fixed-structure tasks
S.detail: Fixed subgoal order and directly localizable objects: planner-free replay reaches 72.63% (581/800) vs 62.50% for a planner without reasoning, with 56.17 s tool time (2607.08448#s3).

F.name: Memory mined from or selected on the evaluation tasks
F.detail: The skill library is mined from evaluation-task rollouts in a single pass; the best replay card is selected on the reporting seeds; tasks without a successful source trace score 0 (2603.22435#s2, 2607.08448#s3).

F.name: Novel or partially observable tasks untested
F.detail: Experience notes are not shown for partially observable or novel tasks, and in-episode memory gives no benefit under full observability (2606.10267#s3).

F.name: Cumulative, single-run memory ablations
F.detail: The scene graph adds only +1 SR on ObjectNav in a cumulative single-run ablation; only the automatic context window is ablated, on 18 cases (2609.15195#s2, 2609.29389#s3).

F.name: Stored content can mislead
F.detail: Seed skills can hurt (Goal Pos. 30.0 -> 26.7); a task-progress record may carry a wrong judgement forward (2609.29964#s2, 2606.10577#s3).

F.name: Bootstrapping needs privileged resets
F.detail: Notes are bootstrapped with a RESET primitive, a generous budget and the benchmark success predicate; task vs global memory are not separated (2607.08448#s2).

S.name: Harness unchanged from training to deployment
S.detail: Harness-native RL lifts one 4B model on SWE-bench Verified from 3.8 -> 26.4 under an unfamiliar harness and 34.2 -> 40.4 under another (2605.24220#s1); per-harness gains +6.4/+5.8/+9.4 (2608.17393#s3); with SFT initialization a robot planner goes 65.1% -> 71.0% (sign test p=0.001 on 121 vs 74 discordant episodes) (2610.28589#s2).

S.name: Token-exact capture
S.detail: Median Pearson between rollout and trainer logprobs is at least 0.998 per scaffold (2608.17393#s1); rollout-level advantage with exact-prefix merges reaches 38.2% vs 35.0% and 33.1% validation reward (2608.17528#s2).

S.name: Rollout-level assembly
S.detail: Prefix-chain assembly cuts trainer updates 1,185 -> 218 and wall-clock 189.5 -> 35.2 min (5.39x) over the same 3 steps (2605.24220#s2).

S.name: Intermediate-difficulty pool and leakage defenses
S.detail: Before defenses, git-history reads (4.6-20.5%) and test edits (2.4-19.4%) hack the reward; screened difficulty bands reach 0.670-0.671 validation while the unscreened pool (72.7% never solved) does not improve (2608.17393#s2).

S.name: Training uses the deployment context rules
S.detail: Training under the deployment compression rule reaches 37.8% vs 33.0% at 53% input cost (2608.03327#s3); the same prompt/history/schema at train and test adds 55.88% -> 71.76% cumulatively (2610.15572#s3); scaffolds stack on a summary-trained policy (8.27 vs 5.02 hourly profit) but not on plain GRPO (2606.14674#s2).

F.name: Little to gain when already aligned
F.detail: Gain is +0.6 when the base model is already harness-aligned; evidence is SWE only (2605.24220#s1).

F.name: Compaction and reserialization break prefix chains
F.detail: Compacted or rewritten histories are dropped; template non-compositionality, retokenize drift and tool-call reserialization break prefixes, and only 36% of coding rollouts stay a single row (2608.17393#s1, 2608.17528#s1).

F.name: Gains do not carry across harnesses
F.detail: A model gains +3.4 under one harness and -0.4 under another; cross-harness transfer of a trained checkpoint is not reported (2608.17393#s3).

F.name: Zero-variation groups grow
F.detail: All-0/all-1 groups rise from 44.7% to 51.4% as the policy improves; binary reward cannot credit recovery; defenses cover only observed failures (2608.17393#s2).

F.name: Embodied rollouts inherit teacher gaps at high cost
F.detail: 2,304 episodes of up to 7,200 s each; suites where the teacher rarely succeeds stay low after RL (2610.28589#s2).

F.name: Alignment gains in-distribution only
F.detail: Held-out accuracy under compression is unchanged and a pre-registered +15 pp bar was not met; scaffold-alignment differences may be within noise (2608.03327#s3, 2606.14674#s2).

S.name: Raw traces given to the optimizer
S.detail: The optimizer sees code, scores and raw traces: median/best accuracy 50.0/56.7 vs 34.6/41.3 with scores only (2603.28052#s2); full 76.7 vs 70.0 without traces and 63.3 with score only (2610.08432#s1).

S.name: Search set separate from a reported held-out set
S.detail: 27B held-out navigation 66.0 -> 75.3 and manipulation 26.4 -> 39.4, above one-shot harness rewrites (75.3 vs 67.7/65.7) (2610.08432#s1); 48.6% vs 40.9 on online text classification with 11.4K vs 50.8K context tokens (2603.28052#s1).

S.name: Revision accepted on the recipient's success
S.detail: Playbook length and dev-rollout limits are held equal and evaluation uses held-out initial configurations: a teacher-refined playbook lifts the light agent 31.3% -> 66.7%, at $0.63 vs $3.43 per episode for the teacher (2609.33378#s2).

S.name: Gated alternation compared with ungated and single-component baselines
S.detail: A validation gate beats ungated alternation 45.26 vs 40.67 and 75.19 vs 68.25, rejecting 17 regressions among 44 proposals (2609.37105#s2); joint adaptation 45.26% vs RL-only 38.83% (2609.37105#s1); candidates compared under the same checkpoint give 44.9% vs 41.7% for a harness searched with the base policy fixed (2610.28069#s2).

F.name: Harness overfits the search split
F.detail: The best search-set harness is not always best on held-out data, and held-out scores plateau or decline; on one benchmark the search set equals the test set (2610.08432#s1, 2603.28052#s1).

F.name: Gains on recurring tasks with ground-truth feedback
F.detail: Success 72% -> 98% (R2R) over ten passes on the same recurring 100-task subsets; EQA varies non-monotonically across passes (2609.39207#s3).

F.name: Point-estimate gate on small validation sets
F.detail: 53-58 validation tasks reused across rounds; the acceptance rule is not a significance test; weight stages can reduce the validation score; one training run per condition (2609.37105#s2, 2609.37105#s1, 2610.28069#s2).

F.name: Rollout bill
F.detail: 18,056 rollouts vs 16,928 for GRPO plus teacher calls; 184-rollout-per-side comparisons would be far costlier with embodied rollouts (2610.28069#s2).

F.name: Unrefined or self-refined playbooks hurt
F.detail: The initial playbook gives 31.3%, below no playbook (43.8%); self-refinement by the light agent gives 22.9%; the acceptance rule does not guarantee termination (2609.33378#s2).

F.name: One harness for heterogeneous subtasks
F.detail: A shared manipulation harness stays below separately optimized ones (held-out 33.8 vs 40.7) (2610.08432#s2).

S.name: Corrections validated before training
S.detail: At the same data budget, first-error repair beats BC (46.1 vs 43.0) (2509.14257#s1); three verified patches give 46/50 vs 3/50 for success-filtered teacher demonstrations (2609.32416#s3); teacher edits rewritten in the student's style give 41.1% vs 17.5% for off-policy teacher takeover (2610.19834#s1).

S.name: Capable reviewer at every step
S.detail: Per-step review and replacement under the minimal harness averages 81.1% vs 78.1% (code-as-harness) and 68.6% (minimal harness) (2609.24974#s1); the distilled student's macro average rises 23.3 -> 44.3, above the base model under the evolved harness (41.7) (2609.24974#s3).

S.name: Gate cuts teacher queries
S.detail: The teacher is queried on 1.2-13.3% of training steps, 7.5x-86x fewer calls than full-query baselines, and not at deployment (2609.01567#s1).

S.name: Relabel where dynamics are near-deterministic
S.detail: Online distillation reaches the best return under deterministic dynamics while RL wins under higher motor noise (2510.03207#s1); relabeling with recovery raises full-chunk SR 16.45% -> 63.46% (seen) (2610.21450#s1).

S.name: RL restarted from correction states
S.detail: Compute-matched, RL from verified prefixes reaches 52.3 avg vs 48.4 without short-horizon starts (2509.14257#s2); resets to teacher-reached states give near-perfect success on three simulated tasks and 100% on 12 real drawer-search episodes (2505.09546#s2).

F.name: Teacher weak where the student fails
F.detail: Weaker editor teachers give weaker students (33.3% and 26.9% vs 41.1%); weaker reviewers are net harmful (-12.0 pp while replacing 66% of steps); a random teacher degrades training (2610.19834#s1, 2609.24974#s1, 2609.01567#s1).

F.name: Verification, review and reset cost
F.detail: >=4,192 suffix rollouts for 19 admissions with snapshot restore; per-step review roughly doubles latency (237.2 s vs 100.1 s per trial) (2609.32416#s1, 2609.24974#s1).

F.name: Seed variance and thin admissions
F.detail: Trainer-seed variance is large (spill 50/33/33); a refinement with one thin admission regressed 76% -> 58%; pooling tasks causes interference (2609.32416#s2).

F.name: Information-gathering regime excluded
F.detail: The distill-vs-RL theory excludes active information gathering; early termination remains dominant after relabeling (21-37%) (2510.03207#s1, 2610.21450#s1).

F.name: Gate signal confounded
F.detail: Entropy conflates uncertainty with multimodality; early discriminator errors misclassify states and a too-strong discriminator increases aliasing (2609.01567#s1, 2505.09546#s1).

F.name: Fully observable text domains only
F.detail: The review ablation runs on one domain with a single seed; live-web success stays below 8%; text/tool sandboxes are fully observable (2609.24974#s3, 2610.19834#s1).

S.name: Interface elements swapped with the backbone fixed
S.detail: One interface element is changed while the model stays fixed: replacing the target-plus-planner action tool with a waypoint predictor lowers R2R-CE SR/SPL 76/66.50 -> 66/57.73, and removing the depth tool gives SR 60 vs 76 (depth-image input instead: 69) (2606.10577#s1, 2606.10577#s2); compact LM-oriented commands beat shell-only interaction 18.0% vs 11.0% on SWE-bench Lite with one model (2405.15793#s1).

S.name: Observation calls do not advance the world; actions report achieved motion
S.detail: Observe and reasoning tools leave the simulator where it is, action tools return achieved motion and residual error, and turn and wall-clock caps are stated; a minimal observe/step interface reaches R2R-CE-100 SR 75.7 +/- 1.5 (medium) and 81.3 +/- 2.5 (ultra effort) over 3 runs each (2607.26148#s1, 2609.29861#s1, 2609.29389#s1).

S.name: Geometry stays inside tools on calibrated metric depth
S.detail: Depth, point clouds, calibration and maps are held by tools; the model gets receipts (depth statistics, measured points, plane fits, map boxes) or picks a target the tool back-projects; the depth is calibrated and metric. A perception-augmented interface lifts a paired 18-trial comparison 61.1% -> 88.9%, and map entries are verified by close-range perception (2606.10577#s2, 2609.29389#s1, 2610.12549#s3, 2609.29964#s1).

S.name: Semantic vocabulary follows embodiment conventions over a reliable executor
S.detail: Model output is restricted to semantic units or entity calls that an interpreter or frozen point-goal navigator executes; units follow motion conventions (arbitrary symbols succeed 1/20), and a scene-graph entity interface reaches 39.7% SR / 19.7% SPL on 3000 HM3D-OVON val_unseen episodes (2609.10522#s1, 2606.27871#s1).

S.name: Extra tools are optional and checked per backbone
S.detail: Tools are added beside primitives rather than replacing them, harness parse/coordinate/feedback correctness is verified before comparison, and effects are reported per model: optional hybrid tools raise the strongest model 82.3 -> 85.7 SR at 0.59x calls, while imposed waypoints lift weak models (5 -> 43 SR) and move strong ones by <=2 points (2607.26148#s2, 2608.03327#s1).

S.name: Image-to-text conversion compared with raw images
S.detail: A separate VLM's text (visual differencing or grounded descriptions) is compared against raw RGB in the same loop: text differencing beats raw image interleaving, which degrades relative to text-only feedback; bounding-box and contact-grounded descriptions reach 47.90% / 52.36% vs 38.84% image-only long-horizon success (2603.22435#s1, 2606.10267#s2).

F.name: Wrong stop and wrong target dominate what is left
F.detail: Residual failures are wrong target/route and wrong stop (15/44 each in one 126-failure audit), runs that enter the goal radius but stop elsewhere, and 8/100 tasks failing in all six runs (2607.26148#s1, 2609.29861#s1).

F.name: Requested rather than realized motion
F.detail: Step returns report requested motion: forward batches stall with pixel-identical views and inconsistent recovery, and on a physical quadruped the agent under-rotates without realized-motion feedback and lacks body awareness (2609.29861#s1, 2607.26148#s1).

F.name: Depth assumption untested
F.detail: Tools assume calibrated metric depth and targets are restricted to visible pixels with valid depth; behaviour under non-metric or scene-dependent depth scaling is untested (2606.10577#s2, 2606.10577#s1).

F.name: Interface bundle compared instead of components
F.detail: A paired comparison changes perception, memory, motion and completion feedback together on 18 trials; no harness-component ablation for scene-graph entity calls; contact views, rehearsal and drag correction are not ablated separately (2609.29389#s1, 2606.27871#s1, 2609.29964#s1).

F.name: Tool value depends on the backbone
F.detail: The same tool helps weak and not strong models; injecting MCP tools gives +4.0 pp for a thinking checkpoint and -5.9 pp for an instruct one, and the two checkpoints differ in more than reasoning (2607.26148#s2, 2608.03327#s1).

F.name: Gain carried by the converter or a privileged channel
F.detail: No VLM-backbone ablation separates the converter's own capability, and wall time roughly doubles (cube stack 60.8 s -> 113.6 s); the best description variant relies on simulator-privileged contact information unavailable on the real robot (2603.22435#s1, 2606.10267#s2).

F.name: Latency and contamination unaccounted
F.detail: 3-19 s per call and high inference cost; benchmark contamination of proprietary models cannot be verified; mostly single runs on 100-episode subsets (2607.26148#s1, 2609.29861#s1).

S.name: Student keeps the full harness, with the three-row comparison
S.detail: Teacher, untrained student and distilled student are reported in the identical harness: a 4B student reaches 87.1% sim success (base 22.2%, teacher 90.4%) and 90.0% real (teacher 93.3%), with call latency 4.168 s -> 0.587 s (2606.18363#s3).

S.name: Hundreds of success-filtered decisions
S.detail: About 500 decision samples or about 110 episodes are used; the student rises 21% -> 43-47% SR and queries per episode fall 30.61 -> 9.41 (2606.27871#s2, 2609.29389#s2, 2609.29964#s3).

S.name: Verified checkpoint branches compared at equal dataset size
S.detail: With teacher success about 90%, perturbation branches at equal dataset size (2,268) raise overall success 79.3% -> 87.1% and unseen tasks 77.1% -> 90.8% (2606.18363#s2); verified branches lift a VLA 18% -> 69% mean success from 10 to 400 demos (2609.27308#s3).

S.name: Removed components handled explicitly
S.detail: Teacher turns that depend on a removed component are rewritten and filtered: 64.6% vs 55.2% for mask-only, SFT 18.1% -> 65.1% (2610.28589#s1); demonstrations share the student's semantic unit space (2609.10522#s3).

F.name: Student does not run standalone
F.detail: Sub-agents remain frontier calls at evaluation; without the frontier planner the student gets 10% on reasoning-intensive tasks (2609.29964#s3, 2609.10522#s3).

F.name: Only teacher-visited states supervised
F.detail: Held-out-task accuracy stays at 13.9% with success-filtered teacher data; recovery supervision comes from teacher-visited perturbed states, not student-induced ones; privileged execution during collection leaves real-executor states uncovered, with no on-policy correction (2609.29389#s2, 2606.18363#s2, 2606.27871#s2).

F.name: Teacher quality does not predict student quality
F.detail: Mixing teachers hurt (41%), and the stronger teacher (56%) yields the weaker student (41% vs 43%) (2606.27871#s2).

F.name: Evaluated on the training tasks
F.detail: Evaluation uses the same tasks with new initial states or new seeds (2610.28589#s1, 2609.29964#s3).

F.name: Branch data can hurt seen tasks
F.detail: Some seen tasks drop with perturbation data (push basket 86.7 -> 66.7, shell game 70.0 -> 63.3) (2606.18363#s2).

F.name: Small end-to-end coverage
F.detail: Only six tasks reach VLA training, the pipeline is never run end to end, and real full-task success is 20% (2609.27308#s3).

S.name: White-box logits with reverse KL
S.detail: LIBERO average 48.9% -> 87.4% (distill) and 93.4% (distill + GRPO) vs teacher 93.9% (2603.26666#s1); reverse KL improves steadily where forward KL drops >50% early and hard-CE plateaus lowest (2603.26666#s2).

S.name: Information-rich privilege at moderate divergence
S.detail: Privileged self-distillation reaches 37.5% vs RL 27.5% on TravelPlanner (2602.04942#s2); next-screenshot privilege adds +3.17 over an unprivileged teacher, with AndroidWorld 52.73 vs GRPO 47.13 over 3 seeds (2608.06065#s1).

S.name: Joint, interleaved privileged and plain views
S.detail: Joint T+I+R training gives 22.98% vs 20.58% task success, while a staged schedule collapses to 7.03% (2610.20261#s2); joint training reaches 44.1% vs 32.3% for SFT+RL (2602.04942#s1).

S.name: Privileged-self targets verified by the harness
S.detail: Verified privileged-self targets give 20.58% vs 15.61% (OPD), 7.72% (GSPO) and 2.06% (SFT on ground truth) (2610.20261#s1).

S.name: Agreement reward with commit-best continuation
S.detail: OOD average +5.1/+6.9 pp for a 4B student with two teachers (2610.19820#s1); replacing commit-best with random commit lowers pass^1 40.0 -> 37.5 (2610.19820#s2).

S.name: Harness-contrast preference with a validity filter
S.detail: ALFWorld unseen 63.4% vs 47.0% best OPD baseline, above the 8B teacher (2610.02858#s1); removing the validity filter lowers average SR 57.4 -> 50.8 (2610.02858#s2).

F.name: Teacher ceiling and teacher access
F.detail: The distilled student stays below its teacher and the method needs logits, so black-box API teachers are excluded; agreement-trained students remain far below teachers (37.7 vs 71.2) (2603.26666#s1, 2610.19820#s1).

F.name: Weak, uninterpretable or over-strong privilege
F.detail: Reference action alone as privilege gives 58.62 vs SFT 59.05; negative privilege utility makes student-only training fail; excessive KL overrides utility and degrades OOD on a smaller model (2608.06065#s1, 2602.04942#s1, 2602.04942#s2).

F.name: Schedules collapse
F.detail: Teacher-only training collapses when KL nears zero and no single mixing weight is best; staged schedules degrade closed-loop success (2602.04942#s1, 2610.20261#s2).

F.name: Agreement or validity is not correctness
F.detail: Matcher false positives/negatives misassign reward and teacher errors become targets; valid-but-incorrect positives cannot be filtered (2610.19820#s1, 2610.02858#s2).

F.name: Holding state makes visitation off-policy
F.detail: Rolling several candidates from one held state introduces off-policy state visitation (2610.19820#s2).

F.name: Small gains outside one text environment
F.detail: WebShop SR 19.6 vs 19.0; untested on multimodal, embodied, long-horizon or partially observed physical tasks (2610.02858#s1, 2608.06065#s1).

S.name: Code composition compared at a matched call budget
S.detail: Same model, primitives, tasks and LLM-call budget: code cells raise success 63.1% -> 71.7%, and on jointly solved instances cut LLM calls 17.0 -> 8.7, input tokens 788k -> 276k and cost $1.63 -> $0.74 (2610.01939#s1).

S.name: Minimal calibrated geometry library
S.detail: A minimal geometric library with known calibration reaches 51.6% average SR on 2,100 episodes, 2.3x direct end-effector control by the same model, and 52.9% mean over 3 seeds (s.d. 0.35) with simulator depth (2610.01939#s2).

S.name: Generated motion validated before execution
S.detail: Generated motion passes MuJoCo/kinematic checks and a safety validation layer before execution, with replay-based repair (2609.39207#s1).

S.name: Frozen VLA staged into its competent regime
S.detail: The planner stages a frozen, in-distribution-competent VLA into a pre-contact state with a stop predicate: the same frozen VLA goes LIBERO-Pro 50.0% -> 72.1-92.63% depending on the planner while standard LIBERO is preserved (96.0 vs 95.3) (2607.08448#s1); candidates are inspected without advancing the environment (2609.33378#s1).

S.name: Tool policy trained for the call it receives
S.detail: Demonstrations are segmented into invocation windows with a data-derived tool taxonomy; tool-aligned post-training plus the interface reaches 95.6/97.2 vs 80.2/80.4 for the interface alone on LIBERO-Long (2605.13119#s1).

F.name: Contact without feedback
F.detail: Button presses and tight fits stay unsolved where pretrained policies reach 83-96%; failures concentrate on contact relative to perception accuracy (2610.01939#s2).

F.name: Mechanism not isolated and budget endings counted as failures
F.detail: Composition, persistent state and selective feedback are not separated; 52 of 96 code-only successes are tool-calling budget exhaustion, and including failures the cost is about equal on one suite (2610.01939#s1).

F.name: Planner backbone swings results with the harness fixed
F.detail: LIBERO-Pro 72.1 vs 82.4 vs 92.63 across planners; Composite-Unseen stays at 13.8-15.0%; analytic primitives and the VLA call are not ablated separately (2607.08448#s1).

F.name: Learned tool helps weak backends only
F.detail: A learned navigation tool adds +11 pp SR for one backend, while the strongest backend drops on RxR (93 -> 86); it is trained for atomic behaviours, not global exploration (2609.39207#s2).

F.name: Unguided access to a frozen policy
F.detail: Tool access without a playbook gives 0/75 on the real robot; instruction and attention edits are unreliable on a task-specific fine-tuned VLA (2609.33378#s1).

F.name: Tool coverage gaps
F.detail: Invocation-aligned post-training first reduced the base VLA 93.4 -> 91.2; primitives absent from the data need new demonstrations; the progress target is a temporal proxy (2605.13119#s1).

F.name: Real-world evidence qualitative
F.detail: Real humanoid tasks take 10-20 minutes and are reported qualitatively (2609.39207#s1).

S.name: Privilege raises teacher coverage
S.detail: LLM revision of the program teacher gives at least one success on all 57 LIBERO-PRO tasks, vs 12 of 57 with no success without revision (2609.21650#s1); full-state coding agents reach up to 82% success (2609.27308#s1).

S.name: Supervision emitted in the student's action vocabulary
S.detail: A rule teacher acting in the student's skills with templated reasoning: 69.6% at 28,480 examples vs 38.8% for 152,478 trajectory-relabeled examples, 71.76% full-task vs 21.90% (2610.15572#s1); spatial-reasoning labels add 65.88% -> 71.76% on the same data (2610.15572#s2).

S.name: Estimate the expert's inputs instead of cloning its actions
S.detail: At a matched 40k-step budget, estimators feeding a frozen expert beat pixel BC (PandaCube 99.0% vs 6.1%, AllegroCube 79.2% vs 0.7%) and transfer to a real arm at 76% (19/25) (2609.34018#s1); a linear state-to-action loss ramp raises TrayPlate 28.9% -> 64.1% (2609.34018#s2).

F.name: Teacher hacks the scorer
F.detail: Full-state coding agents hack the scorer (43% and 39% for two models), over-commit to failing decompositions and leave the hardest tasks unsolved (2609.27308#s1).

F.name: Identifiability unchecked
F.detail: No check whether templated privileged descriptions (e.g. out-of-view direction) are identifiable from student observations; replacing privileged inputs with learned perception is untested (2610.15572#s2, 2609.21650#s1).

F.name: Teacher diversity bounds the student
F.detail: Generalization is bounded by teacher data diversity; real robot 38% end to end; only short single-room navigation; no on-policy correction (2610.15572#s1).

F.name: Loss schedule fragile
F.detail: An abrupt switch or flat action weight collapses (<4% on tray tasks); action-only training converges in 1 of 3 seeds (2609.34018#s2).

F.name: Advantage shrinks with more budget
F.detail: With 3x budget a full-state flow clone closes much of the gap on reaching and tray tasks; most pixel-BC cells are single-seed (2609.34018#s1).

F.name: Single-primitive scope
F.detail: Multi-step tasks are unsupported and the enforced top-down grasp fits box-shaped objects (2609.21650#s1).

S.name: Every task starts with nonzero success
S.detail: Teacher-derived SFT covers 57/57 tasks; after PPO 97.8%/97.1% vs 41.9%/68.4% for matched direct PPO, and zero-success initializations end at 26.0% vs 91.7% (2609.21650#s2); a recovery-DAgger initialization adds +10.72 SR with RL (2610.21450#s2).

S.name: Teacher-free RL with frozen components and one model size
S.detail: RL inside the code harness raises unseen instances 18.8% -> 44.1% and cuts context overflows 19.2% -> 3.4% (2610.01939#s3); privileged perception during training avoids noisy rewards (Cube Lift 80%) (2603.22435#s4).

S.name: Dense forked-branch reward after an SFT warm start
S.detail: Forked stepwise GRPO keeps SR (49% vs 47%) while cutting tokens per query 72.1% and on-device latency 71.8% (2606.27871#s3).

S.name: Rollout hints that do not reveal the answer
S.detail: Mechanism skills injected only in rollouts give 38.3% vs GRPO 35.3% without hints at evaluation, and 46.5% vs 39.0% mixed-outcome groups (2610.28069#s1).

F.name: BC initialization or zero-success start stalls
F.detail: BC-initialized Flow-GRPO stays at 19-26% SR (2610.21450#s2); direct PPO leaves 17 of 27 zero-success tasks at 0% and drives 3 solved tasks to 0% (2609.21650#s2).

F.name: Far below the teacher
F.detail: The RL-trained small model stays at 45.9% vs 71.7% for the frontier model, with more give-ups (25.2%) (2610.01939#s3).

F.name: No held-out evaluation
F.detail: Training-set numbers only (success 2.7% -> 7.5%) (2609.27308#s4); three simple tasks trained per task, with S2 rewards noisy enough for credit-assignment ambiguity (2603.22435#s4).

F.name: Near-answer hints hurt
F.detail: Hints that approach the answer raise training success but lower no-hint evaluation (-2.6 pp vs GRPO) (2610.28069#s1).

F.name: Per-step bandit credit and forking
F.detail: Greedy best-branch continuation is per-step, not full-episode credit; it needs simulator forking and privileged distance-to-goal; text (41%) and table (36%) disagree (2606.27871#s3).

F.name: Coverage effect not isolated; stop timing remains
F.detail: Coverage and difficulty co-vary, real closed-loop transfer failed (2609.21650#s2); late termination increases and stop timing remains the main residual failure (2610.21450#s2).
